title: Standard Operating Procedure for Culturing Bordetella species from Nasopharyngeal Specimens
author: Adria D. Lee
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kq9cvz6

steps.title: Prepare Specimen Split
steps.instruction: Prepare the nasopharyngeal swab for culture and PCR processing.

substeps.instruction: Use sterilized tweezers to hold the swab shaft and remove the swab from the transport media.
Submerge the swab tip in 500μl of 0.85% sterile saline.
Cut the swab shaft above the top of the centrifuge tube using sterilized scissors.

steps.title: Homogenize Specimen
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube and incubate for approximately 2 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Aliquot Specimen for Testing
steps.instruction: Divide the processed specimen into volumes for culture and PCR.

substeps.instruction: Remove 400μl for PCR testing (200μl for extraction).

steps.title: Inoculate Agar Plates
steps.instruction: Inoculate Regan-Lowe agar plates with and without cephalexin (RL+C and RL-C).

substeps.instruction: Using a pipette (or transfer pipette for viscous specimens), inoculate one RL+C and one RL-C agar plate with 50μl of the specimen each.
Using a sterile loop, streak the inoculum in the first quadrant of the plate until all liquid is absorbed.

steps.title: Incubate and Monitor Growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates and monitor for characteristic colony growth.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 37°C with high humidity for 7-10 days.
Examine plates daily using a dissecting microscope and oblique illumination.
Compare colonies against a quality control strain, noting that typical colonies rarely appear before 48-72 hours.

steps.title: Subculture Bordetella-like Organisms
steps.instruction: Isolate and subculture suspected Bordetella-like organisms (BLO).

substeps.instruction: Streak the picked colonies onto RL-C and blood agar.
Incubate for 1-3 days until sufficient growth is achieved for phenotypic testing.
